Под ultimatum человек либо exits сам (`раз так не доверяешь, я уйду`), либо outwardly compliances без internal change. PIP for plateau (не для performance issue) is misuse of formal process.
sections.source_of_confusion: Менеджеру кажется, что pressure motivates. Также corporate culture с up-or-out (consulting, some FAANG levels) предлагает похожий model.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда compositive companies использовали бы PIPs proactively для plateau. Реально PIP — это легальный инструмент для documented performance issues, и его misuse for non-performance reasons рекомендации lawsuits.
sections.how_it_should_be: Если performance fine на текущем уровне, нет grounds для PIP. Если performance below expectation, then proper PIP с clear documented gaps и improvement plan. Не путать plateau preference с performance issue.

options.label: C
options.text: Перевести в другую команду — `свежий воздух` сам решит проблему.

sections.what_actually: Team change может помочь, если plateau связан со specific dynamics или mismatch с current team, но это не universal cure. Человек, который retreats from visibility в команде A, скорее всего так же retreats в команде B без addressing root cause. Forced move без employee buy-in — добавляет stress, не resolves.
sections.source_of_confusion: Move feels like proactive action, и менеджеру это легче, чем coaching через diagnosis. Также есть мнение, что `новое окружение мотивирует`.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда HR rotational programs автоматически solved plateau. Реально rotation помогает selectively, но only when paired with clear development plan и employee agreement.
sections.how_it_should_be: Team change — option in conversation, не unilateral decision. Diagnose сначала root cause; если current team — главный contributor, тогда move с employee agreement и growth plan.

options.label: D
options.text: Принять как есть — не все растут, и команде нужны стабильные исполнители.

sections.what_actually: Passive acceptance — это abdication of mentorship. Если plateau — preference (см. Q12), это легитимно, но требует horizontal growth conversation. Если plateau — fear или skill gap (как в данном scenario с symptomами), passive acceptance закрепляет проблему. Команде нужны не stable plateaus, а growing engineers; иначе skills деградируют relative to market.
sections.source_of_confusion: Менеджеру easier accept than coach through. Также wisdom-sounding aphorisms (`не все растут одинаково`) рационализуют avoidance.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда mentorship не имел бы measurable impact на career progression. Реально McKinsey 2020 показывает: structured mentorship даёт 25% higher internal promotion rates.
sections.how_it_should_be: Не принимать пассивно symptoms of self-imposed limits. Diagnose, intervene, support — это работа менеджера. Принять — только если genuine preference после thorough conversation.

blocks.question_text: Менти готовится к promo (например, middle → senior). Как правильно помочь?

options.label: A
options.text: Совместно посмотреть grade-matrix, определить конкретные пробелы, создать план `доказательств` (проекты, артефакты), дать visibility, помочь со self-review.

sections.explanation: Promo — это признание уже выполняемой работы на новом уровне, не аванс. Принцип: к moment of promo committee menti уже должен behaving as next-level engineer 3-6 месяцев. Подход — пятиэтапный. Первый — calibration через grade-matrix: совместно посмотреть expectations next level (system design, mentorship, cross-team collaboration, technical ownership) и compared с текущим evidence. Чёткие gaps emerge. Второй — план `доказательств`: конкретные projects, RFCs, mentorship engagements, tech talks, cross-team contributions, которые накопят evidence в течение 3-6 месяцев. Третий — visibility: introduce менти к other teams и senior leaders, sponsor его на cross-team projects, encourage public artifacts (RFCs, blog posts, conference talks внутренние). Promo committees решают на basis of visible impact, не invisible. Четвёртый — sponsorship: менеджер советует stay support to menti, говорит про него positively с other managers, активно advocates on promo committee. Пятый — self-review prep: помочь menti structure его promo packet, articulate impact в terms of business outcomes, prepare для cross-functional feedback collection.
sections.example: У Stripe public Engineering Levels с detailed expectations per level. Перед promo конкретный template `Promotion Packet`: highlights with quantified impact, technical artifacts, peer testimonials. У Google `perf` система формализованная: nominations, evidence, calibration meetings. Camille Fournier описывает sponsor role: `you're not just preparing them — you're publicly investing reputation in them`.
sections.when_to_apply: Для 6-12 months pre-promo period; для transitions junior→middle, middle→senior, senior→staff. Особенно critical для senior→staff transition, который часто провалится из-за missing cross-team influence evidence.
sections.edge_cases: Не overpromise. Если evidence не накапливается за target period, лучше реалистично перенести promo, чем `протолкнуть` и иметь PIP через год. Также: promo timelines vary by company; в FAANG senior promo может занять 1.5-3 года; в стартапах быстрее, но критерии могут быть менее clear. Calibrate expectations.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q9]] career tracks по уровням; [[mentoring-interview#Q3]] IDP creation; [[mentoring-interview#Q10]] performance review.

options.label: B
options.text: Просто подать на promo committee — пусть они решают по merits.

sections.what_actually: Passive submission rarely works. Promo committees evaluate documented evidence, не raw potential. Без prepared packet, visibility, sponsorship — даже good engineer часто rejected с feedback `not enough cross-team impact` или `need more visible technical leadership`. Это месяцы delays.
sections.source_of_confusion: Идея `merit-based promotion` подсознательно suggests `let the best win on objective evidence`. Реально even merit-based systems require prepared evidence; raw talent invisible без presentation.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда promo committees passed on raw work products without curated packets. Реально committees rely on submitted documentation: highlights, artifacts, testimonials.
sections.how_it_should_be: Active preparation: evidence accumulation, visibility, sponsorship, packet curation. Это not gaming the system — это helping committee see your case.

options.label: C
options.text: Дать менти complex задачу прямо перед review — `last moment evidence`.

sections.what_actually: Crash project для evidence — это antipattern. Cannot accumulate sufficient depth и cross-team impact за пару месяцев. Часто такие проекты под pressure failing or completing с rough edges, что counterproductive. Promo committee видит pattern over time, не single project.
sections.source_of_confusion: Менеджеру feels like proactive last-minute push. Также есть мнение, что `один heroic effort` show level capabilities.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда promo committees promoted based on last project. Реально committees evaluate sustained pattern across multiple quarters.
sections.how_it_should_be: Long-term consistent evidence: project portfolio over 6-12 months, многократно proven patterns, sustained mentorship engagement, cross-team work spread across quarters.

options.label: D
options.text: Если менти готов — promo автоматический; помощь не нужна.

sections.what_actually: Promo не автоматический. Даже at-level performance requires deliberate packaging, advocacy, и cross-functional buy-in. Особенно for senior+ levels с calibration committees или promotion boards.
sections.source_of_confusion: Идея `talent will out` популярна, но she meritocratic systems still require advocacy. Sponsorship research (Hewlett 2013) показала: people с active sponsor 23% more likely получить promotion, чем equivalents без.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда sponsorship не имел бы measurable impact. Реально active sponsorship — один из top predictors of career advancement, особенно для underrepresented groups.
sections.how_it_should_be: Active mentor + sponsor role: preparation, packet, visibility, advocacy. Это не nepotism, это enabling deserving people to be seen.

blocks.question_text: Как трекать прогресс менти между 1:1 встречами?

options.label: A
options.text: Общий running document с 1:1 notes, quarterly goals с чекпойнтами, промежуточные артефакты (RFC, статья, тех-таск).

sections.explanation: Tracking progress без micromanagement требует баланса между visibility и autonomy. Лучший механизм — shared running document, который ведёт менти, а ментор только commentates. Структура документа: agenda для предстоящего 1:1, краткие notes с предыдущего (что обсудили, что договорились), список текущих focus areas с deliverables, quarterly goals с status (on track, blocked, completed). Менти заполняет до встречи (agenda), вы оба обновляете во время (notes, agreements), и менти tracks между встречами. Quarterly goals — это OKRs lite: 2-3 measurable outcomes, не 10. Каждое имеет concrete artifact (RFC published, system designed, mentorship initiated, tech talk delivered). Промежуточные артефакты — лучший proxy progress: artifact с timestamp lets вам see что и когда было сделано. Это лучше abstract metrics типа `time spent learning` — focuses на output, не на input. Признаки good progress: menti сам инициирует agenda items, сам приходит с self-assessment, сам identifies blockers ahead of time. Признаки tracking problem: ничего не обновляется между встречами, agenda пустая, blockers surface only при direct asking.
sections.example: У GitLab handbook publically describes 1:1 template и tracking practice. Notion и Coda стали popular tools для running mentorship docs. У Spotify quarterly review process требует documented evidence of progress against OKRs, что forces visibility между ревью.
sections.when_to_apply: Для всех mentor-mentee pairs starting from day 1. Особенно critical для distributed teams (where casual sync less frequent), для new managers (where pattern not established), для high-stakes preparation (promo, role change).
sections.edge_cases: Не превращайте document в micromanagement tool. Если вы checking documents daily и pushing updates — это surveillance. Document should be checked by mentee, manager sees during 1:1. Также: не over-engineer структуру; simple document with notes более robust than complex multi-page templates.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q2]] 1:1 structure; [[mentoring-interview#Q21]] невыполнение договорённостей; [[mentoring-interview#Q24]] эффективность менторства.

options.label: B
options.text: Проверять JIRA tickets и git commits — это objective progress evidence.

sections.what_actually: Tickets и commits показывают tactical output, не growth. Менти может closing tickets steady, но не расти в leadership, system design, mentorship. Также: focus on tickets reinforces transactional view of work и misses growth dimensions.
sections.source_of_confusion: Tickets/commits — easy quantifiable metrics, и engineers с metric-oriented mindset предпочитают this. Также some managers используют это для proxy productivity.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда engineers с highest commit count были бы highest performers. Реально often quiet, thoughtful contributors с fewer но deeper commits outperform high-commit-count individuals в impact и growth.
sections.how_it_should_be: Track growth indicators: artifacts shipped (RFCs, designs), mentorship engagement, cross-team contributions, leadership behaviours. Commits/tickets useful as supplementary data, not primary.

options.label: C
options.text: Полагаться на quarterly review — между ревью нет необходимости трекать.

sections.what_actually: Tracking only quarterly предполагает surprises на ревью. Это контрпродуктивно: at quarterly evaluation либо progress incomplete (поздно correct), либо blockers identified late (3 месяца лост). Continuous tracking — это early warning system, не just evaluation.
sections.source_of_confusion: Quarterly review feels comprehensive, и менеджерам comfortable thinking `that's когда мы проверяем`. Также tracking effort может seem like overhead.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда annual performance review systems показывали бы лучше outcomes than continuous performance management. Реально companies, перешедшие на continuous PM (Adobe, Microsoft, Deloitte) показывают improvement в engagement и outcomes.
sections.how_it_should_be: Quarterly review — summary of continuous tracking, not first time looking. Surprises на ревью = problem in tracking process. Aim for `no surprises` mantra.

options.label: D
options.text: Спрашивать peer'ов и менеджеров других команд каждую неделю — собирать 360 feedback continuously.

sections.what_actually: Continuous 360 feedback collection — это surveillance pattern. Burns reputation between менти и peers (`зачем мой ментор спрашивает обо мне каждую неделю?`); creates anxiety; consumes peer time. 360 feedback useful for formal reviews, не как continuous tracking mechanism.
sections.source_of_confusion: Idea `external perspective` valuable, и при том правильна для periodic review. Но frequency wrong — weekly creates surveillance feel.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда continuous polling improved outcomes. Реально это decreases trust и creates Hawthorne effect (people change behavior знаючи, что watched).
sections.how_it_should_be: 360 feedback — periodic (semi-annual or annual), formal process. Continuous tracking — through mentee's own document и direct observation в normal work.

blocks.question_text: Менти приходит и говорит: я думаю перейти в другую команду или уйти из компании. Как реагировать?

options.label: A
options.text: Сначала эмоционально удержать (поднять зарплату, пообещать promo) — затем разобраться в причинах.

sections.what_actually: Counter-offer и promised promo как первая реакция — это manipulation, не support. 70-80% людей, принявших counter-offer, всё равно уходят в течение года (Harvard Business Review 2019 data). Reason: причины ухода обычно systemic (career path, manager, culture), а counter-offer addresses только surface symptom (salary).
sections.source_of_confusion: Менеджеру panic - потеря team member impacts его performance metrics. Также corporate processes часто позволяют counter-offers, что закрепляет pattern.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда counter-offers retained долгосрочно. Реально data показывает временную retention с rapid exits через 6-12 months.
sections.how_it_should_be: Сначала understand reasons through honest conversation. Counter-offer — possible, но только если addresses real reasons, не как panic reaction.

options.label: B
options.text: Выяснить причины честно, предложить альтернативы внутри компании, если фит лучше уйти — поддержать с рекомендацией.

sections.explanation: Когда менти shares намерение уйти, primary роль mentor — быть на стороне роста человека, не на стороне retention любой ценой. Подход — четырёхэтапный. Первый — honest diagnosis through open questions: что не работает в текущей роли (boredom, conflict, manager fit), что pull factor в other place (opportunity, money, lifestyle), что бы изменило situation. Important — listen без defensiveness; не interpret as personal failure. Второй — explore internal alternatives, если применимо: другая команда, другая роль, sabbatical, sabbatical, role redesign. Менеджер может facilitate intros, advocate с other teams. Но честно — если internal alternatives не fit, не push them. Третий — если external move best — support через рекомендацию, networking, advice. Это long-term mindset: alumni network — это asset для company и для менеджера. People remember those, who supported them through transitions. Четвёртый — knowledge transfer и professional exit: помочь plan onboarding for replacement, document key context, clean handoffs. Это professional credit для уходящего person.
sections.example: Reid Hoffman (LinkedIn founder) в `The Alliance` описывает employee-employer relationship as tour of duty: people come to grow и contribute, и leave when fit no longer works. Companies, что embrace this, build powerful alumni networks. Stripe, Netflix, Google known for strong alumni networks; people often return after external experience (`boomerang employees`).
sections.when_to_apply: Для любых exit conversations, как с long-tenured так и с new hires. Также для internal team change discussions — same principle applies: support human's growth, не just team's retention. Также: для people considering sabbatical, parental leave extension, или other life transitions.
sections.edge_cases: Не over-promise on internal moves. Если other team не interested или role не available, лучше honest acknowledge than create false hope. Также: be careful с confidentiality — exit discussion confidential; не tell other team members until employee ready. После decision сделать proper send-off — recognition, not awkward exit.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q12]] нет амбиций роста; [[mentoring-interview#Q8]] bored high-performer; [[mentoring-interview#Q1]] mentor as career advisor.

options.label: C
options.text: Усиленно retain любой ценой — потеря члена команды разрушает progress.

sections.what_actually: Retain любой ценой — это short-term thinking. Reluctant employee — это productivity drag и culture risk. Также: reputation manager как someone, кто `traps` people, разрушает trust с rest of команды.
sections.source_of_confusion: Manager's short-term metrics often penalize team member exits, что creates pressure to retain.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда companies с highest retention rates были бы highest performers. Реально healthy turnover в knowledge work 10-15% annually; lower может indicate stagnation, higher — culture problem.
sections.how_it_should_be: Retain when good fit и employee growth supported here. Let go gracefully when fit breaks или employee growth requires external move.

options.label: D
options.text: Игнорировать — пусть уходит, replacement найдётся.

sections.what_actually: Cold response к exit conversation — это immediate reputation hit. Other team members observe и interpret as `manager doesn't care about people`. Outgoing person leaves с negative feeling и shares experience в network. Cost replacement (recruiting, onboarding, productivity lost) обычно $200K-500K — это not trivial.
sections.source_of_confusion: Менеджер might feel hurt или resentful (`они bailing on us`) и suppress engagement as self-protection.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда detailed exit interviews и offboarding processes не существовали бы как best practice. Реально companies invest significantly в graceful exits для cultural и legal reasons.
sections.how_it_should_be: Engaged exit process: honest conversation about reasons, support transition, maintain relationship for alumni network. Even if person leaves, professional and supportive exit benefits both sides.

blocks.question_text: Как балансировать время между менторством и собственной технической работой?

options.label: A
options.text: Заблокировать timeslots для 1:1 заранее, совмещать через pair programming, делегировать senior'ам, говорить `нет` mentorship outside scope.

sections.explanation: Balancing mentorship и IC work — это chronic challenge для tech leads и engineering managers. Решение — четырёхпроговой подход. Первый — calendar blocking: 1:1 встречи блокируются на recurring slots в начале или конце дня, не в середине, чтобы не fragment deep work time. Без блокировки 1:1 либо вытесняются срочными задачами (`перенесём на следующую неделю`), либо вставляются ad-hoc, fragmenting day. Второй — совмещение через pair programming: вы работаете над собственной задачей, но pairing с junior'ом, который learns by observation и participation. Это и mentorship, и IC output одновременно. Особенно работает для system design discussions, debugging sessions, code review of significant changes. Третий — distributed mentorship: senior'ы как mentors для middle/junior; вы становитесь `mentor of mentors`. Это scaling решение, не replacement (см. Q11). Четвёртый — boundaries: уметь говорить `нет` для mentorship request outside your scope. Если у вас и так 5 direct reports plus 3 senior'а в meta-mentorship, заявка mentor stranger из другой компании — possible, но only as space allows. Не feel guilty saying not now.
sections.example: Andy Grove в `High Output Management` описывает manager output = team output + impact on others. Это framework включает mentorship as part of leverage, not separate. У Camille Fournier `The Manager's Path` есть chapter on time management — recommends 70/20/10 split: 70% direct work, 20% mentorship/coaching, 10% organizational/strategic. Numbers vary, но balance principle universal.
sections.when_to_apply: Для всех hybrid roles (tech lead, staff engineer with mentorship, EM-IC blend). Особенно critical при transitioning IC→management, where many fail to adjust time allocation.
sections.edge_cases: Не over-block. Если 1:1 takes 60% времени, вы вряд ли still doing meaningful IC work, и должны honestly choose: либо go full manager, либо reduce direct reports. Также: pair programming не replaces 1:1 — 1:1 still needs dedicated time for sensitive topics.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q11]] масштабирование mentorship; [[mentoring-interview#Q9]] career tracks; [[mentoring-interview#Q2]] 1:1 structure.

options.label: B
options.text: Сократить 1:1 до 15 минут — это spar time без жертв во встречах.

sections.what_actually: 15-минутные 1:1 не дают enough depth для meaningful conversation. Greeting + check-in + brief topic = время up, без real discussion. Лучше 30-45 minutes biweekly than 15 minutes weekly: depth > frequency для mentorship.
sections.source_of_confusion: Time pressure makes short meetings appealing. Также marketing of 15-min stand-ups creates impression `short = efficient`.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда meaningful coaching mostly fits in 15 minutes. Реально research shows meaningful career conversations require 30-60 minutes of focused time.
sections.how_it_should_be: 30-45 minutes biweekly as baseline. If time-pressured, reduce frequency (monthly) before reducing duration. Reducing both — sign of need for distributed mentorship model.

options.label: C
options.text: Полностью отказаться от собственной технической работы — это price of leadership.

sections.what_actually: Complete IC abandonment — это antipattern для tech leads. Без hands-on coding tech lead loses credibility, loses technical instinct, can't effectively mentor on technical issues. Также: many tech leads burn out из-за loss of intrinsic technical joy.
sections.source_of_confusion: Some leadership literature (especially in non-tech contexts) advocates full transition to people management. В tech contexts that's nuanced — many tech leads need preserve hands-on element.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда staff и principal engineers, who do significant hands-on coding while mentoring, would not exist. Реально Will Larson `Staff Engineer` shows multiple archetypes balance both.
sections.how_it_should_be: Adjust balance, не eliminate. For tech lead with team of 5-7: 50% IC, 50% leadership. For EM with team of 10+: 20% IC, 80% leadership. For principal с no direct reports: 80% IC, 20% mentorship/sponsorship.

options.label: D
options.text: Прекратить mentorship на 3 месяца для критичного проекта — потом возобновить.

sections.what_actually: 3-month mentorship pause — это major signal disengagement. Mentees feel abandoned; trust takes long to rebuild. Also: project pressures will recur — pausing раз становится pausing regularly, что де facto eliminates mentorship.
sections.source_of_confusion: В crunch mode менеджер feels guilt о mentorship time как `not real work`. Этот guilt suggests rethinking what `real work` actually is.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда crisis-driven companies не нуждались бы в mentorship structure. Реально even high-pressure environments (Amazon, finance trading) maintain mentorship structure precisely because crisis amplifies mentorship value.
sections.how_it_should_be: Maintain mentorship через crunch periods — maybe shorter sessions, but maintain rhythm. Crisis time is when mentees need support most. Eliminate other things first (status meetings, low-value work).

blocks.question_text: Команда работает над длинным проектом (6+ месяцев) с invisible progress. Мотивация падает. Что делать ментору?

options.label: A
options.text: Разбить на visible milestones, регулярно подводить итоги, связывать с business value, публично признавать вклад.

sections.explanation: Длинные проекты с invisible progress — это motivation killer. Без видимого прогресса dopamine reward loop breaks: люди работают, но не feel achievement. Mentor's role — recreate motivation through artificial structure. Четыре tactics. Первый — milestone decomposition: разбить 6-месячный project на 2-3 weekly visible milestones. Не all milestones обязательно shippable to production — могут быть internal achievement gates (`design completed`, `prototype validated`, `performance benchmarked`). Each milestone celebrated. Второй — regular retrospectives на progress: monthly review показывает, что было выполнено, что было challenging, что узнали. Это externalizes progress, makes it visible. Третий — business value framing: regularly remind team why this matters business-wise. `Мы строим recommendation engine, который увеличит click-through на 15%, что = $5M annually`. Без этого frame technical work feels purely technical. Четвёртый — public recognition: celebrate individual contributions на all-hands, в team channels, в performance reviews. People need to feel that work matters and is seen. Особенно critical для long projects where there's no natural high-visibility moment.
sections.example: У SpaceX projects вроде Starship development organized в visible milestones: `static fire complete`, `hop test passed`, `belly flop demonstrated`, `orbital attempt`. Each celebrated, even when overall project still years from final goal. У NASA Apollo program similarly structured: Mercury → Gemini → Apollo missions create stepping stones over decade. У software projects similar principle: design doc → prototype → MVP → beta → GA.
sections.when_to_apply: Для long-duration projects (3+ months), для research-heavy work without obvious deliverables, для infrastructure projects where impact delayed, для process improvement work where business value not immediately visible.
sections.edge_cases: Не fabricate milestones. People can sense artificial celebration vs genuine achievement. Также: don't over-celebrate small wins — overuse depletes celebration currency. Pace celebration to scale of actual achievement.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q4]] SBI for praise too; [[mentoring-interview#Q14]] стагнация на plateau; [[mentoring-interview#Q7]] impostor syndrome (similar mechanism).

options.label: B
options.text: Усилить давление и дедлайны — это форсирует mobilization.

sections.what_actually: Increased pressure on already-low-motivation team accelerates burnout. People work harder short-term, then crash. Quality drops, turnover increases. Long-term project becomes longer because team disintegrates.
sections.source_of_confusion: Pressure feels actionable; manager can `do something`. Также legacy management belief that fear motivates.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда tightest deadline cultures (game development в late stages, finance during deals) showed best long-term outcomes. Реально these often показывают highest burnout rates и highest turnover post-crunch.
sections.how_it_should_be: Address root cause (invisible progress, lost purpose), not symptom (perceived low velocity). Milestones, retrospectives, business framing — все this restores motivation without burning out team.

options.label: C
options.text: Раз результаты не видны — переключить команду на другой, более `видимый` проект.

sections.what_actually: Project abandonment after months of work — это signal что long-term investments не safe в этой company. Team's sunk cost effort wasted; trust в management decreased; future motivation для long projects undermined. Также: business value of original project не realized.
sections.source_of_confusion: Switching feels proactive. Также short-term metric focus может pressure managers toward visible-near-term over long-term value.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда research labs и infrastructure teams не могли бы exist. Реально long-term technical investments — это competitive advantage для many companies (e.g. Google Search, Amazon AWS infrastructure).
sections.how_it_should_be: Reframe и restructure project for visible progress, не abandon. If business case actually weakening, that's different conversation — но not because team motivation low.

options.label: D
options.text: Игнорировать motivation drop — `профессионалы должны работать независимо от чувств`.

sections.what_actually: Ignoring motivation creates downward spiral: lower motivation → lower quality → more rework → longer project → even lower motivation. Eventually best team members exit, leaving project with weakest contributors.
sections.source_of_confusion: Old-school management belief that emotions don't belong at work. Also some engineers prefer pure technical focus и uncomfortable с motivation conversations.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда high-performance teams showed no manager attention к motivation. Реально Google Project Aristotle and similar research show psychological safety и motivation are top predictors of team performance.
sections.how_it_should_be: Address motivation as core mentor responsibility. Use techniques mentioned: milestones, retrospectives, business framing, recognition. Motivation isn't optional — it's foundation of sustained performance.

blocks.question_text: Команда полностью удалённая. Какие отличия в менторстве?

options.label: A
options.text: Использовать только async коммуникацию — это эффективнее для всех timezone.

sections.what_actually: Async only mentorship миссес critical dimensions. Tone и intent очень easily misread в text; emotional support harder to convey без voice/video. Career conversations work лучше в real-time dialogue, где ментор can probe и menti can think out loud.
sections.source_of_confusion: Async philosophy popular в remote-first companies (Basecamp, GitLab). Это работает для documentation и decision-making, но не universally для mentorship.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда GitLab handbook не recommend regular 1:1 video calls. Реально even pure-async companies maintain video 1:1 for mentorship и hard conversations.
sections.how_it_should_be: Hybrid: async для routine updates, document review, between-meeting context; sync video для 1:1, hard conversations, career discussions, emotional support.

options.label: B
options.text: Более структурированные 1:1 с видео, async фидбэк через docs, чаще check-in вместо реже но дольше, careful с тоном письменного фидбэка.

sections.explanation: Remote mentorship требует specific adjustments относительно in-office. Первое — структура more important than in-office: без random hallway conversations и lunches, all interaction happens в scheduled time, что requires more deliberate structure. Use video 1:1 with cameras on — visual cues compensate for missing in-person observation. Второе — written feedback приходит harder than verbal: tone neutralizes, context lost, читается more harshly. Solution: extra care в word choice, более позитивное framing, более context-setting, и preference для voice/video on sensitive topics. Третье — check-in frequency: short, frequent check-ins (15-min weekly) often better than infrequent long meetings (60-min monthly). Frequency keeps connection alive; duration goes into structured 30-45 min biweekly 1:1. Четвёртое — async tools для mentorship: shared docs с comments для design feedback и code review, Loom video для walkthrough explanations (`record me thinking through your design`), thread в Slack для quick questions. Пятое — be very explicit о emotional state и social glue: `как ты вообще себя чувствуешь?` нужно ask вслух; в офисе это viewable.
sections.example: GitLab handbook publically details remote mentorship practices: required 1:1s, async written reviews, Donut bot для casual peer connections. Automattic (WordPress.com) operates fully remote с structured mentorship через P2 (internal blog). Buffer remote-first since 2015 с public mentorship structures.
sections.when_to_apply: Для fully remote teams; also hybrid teams где mentor и mentee часто различные locations. Также при interim remote periods (pandemic, sick leaves, parental leave with WFH).
sections.edge_cases: Не over-rely on video — `Zoom fatigue` это real. Iterate format: иногда just-audio для walking 1:1 (mentee can walk while talking, lowers anxiety). Также: timezone differences может make sync difficult — find creative compromise (одна стороны occasionally shifts hours, async для routine, sync для critical).
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q2]] 1:1 structure; [[mentoring-interview#Q13]] hard conversations; [[mentoring-interview#Q4]] SBI feedback.

options.label: C
options.text: Удалённость не влияет на менторство — те же подходы, что и в офисе.

sections.what_actually: Remote и in-person mentorship require different practices. In-person allows informal observation, hallway conversations, casual lunch chats — none of which exist remotely. Pretending no difference leads to missing signals и weak mentorship.
sections.source_of_confusion: В early remote work (pre-2020) many managers naively applied office practices remotely, with poor results. Pandemic forced learning.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда remote-first companies не developed specific remote management practices. Реально companies like GitLab, Buffer, Automattic invested heavily in remote-specific approaches.
sections.how_it_should_be: Acknowledge differences and adjust: more structure, explicit communication, video for sync, async for documentation, frequent check-ins, careful tone в written feedback.

options.label: D
options.text: Требовать приходить в офис на 1:1 — личный контакт ничем не заменишь.

sections.what_actually: Forcing office presence когда team remote — это policy contradiction и trust breach. People joined remote role for specific reasons (location, family, lifestyle); forcing into office shows you don't trust remote setup. Also impractical for distributed teams across timezones.
sections.source_of_confusion: Manager preference for in-person interaction может override understanding of team's needs. Also some leadership courses emphasize in-person bonding without modern remote alternatives.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда remote-first companies были бы non-functional. Реально many remote-first companies outperform in-office equivalents (GitLab IPO'd в 2021 with $14B valuation, fully remote).
sections.how_it_should_be: Build effective remote 1:1 with video, structure, frequent connection. Optional in-person retreats (1-2x annually) для cultural bonding, но не require for routine mentorship.

blocks.question_text: Менти регулярно не выполняет договорённости из 1:1 (например, обещанные tech talks, RFC, обучение). Что делать?

options.label: A
options.text: Проверить реалистичность договорённостей; поднять тему напрямую; выяснить блокеры; уменьшить размер шагов; при системности — обсудить серьёзно.

sections.explanation: Невыполнение договорённостей может означать разное, и подход должен зависеть от причины. Первый шаг — self-check on agreement realism. Часто менеджеры назначают amount чрезмерных commitments в 1:1 enthusiasm (`да, сделаю и Х и Y и Z за квартал`), что unrealistic. Если pattern repeats — это сигнал adjust scope в conversations, не push harder. Второй — direct, non-blaming raise: `мы договорились о Х, я не вижу прогресса. Что случилось?`. Не `почему ты не сделал` — это accusatory; `что случилось` — это inquiry. Третий — diagnose blockers: time (other priorities took over), priorities mismatch (mentor's idea, not menti's), confusion (not clear how to start), motivation drop (lost interest), or competing personal life (parental leave, illness). Каждая causes different intervention. Четвёртый — adjust size of step: если commitment too big (`give tech talk to entire company`), break into smaller (`first, present to team`, then `department`). Easier to follow through на smaller commitments, then scale. Пятый — если систематически невыполнение across multiple agreements — это performance signal, и conversation должен elevate в seriousness: `я замечаю pattern, что договорённости не выполняются. Это affects ваш growth и my ability to support you. Что происходит?`. Это not about punishment, это about honest reckoning.
sections.example: В Camille Fournier `The Manager's Path` есть chapter on `the toxic employee` — describes pattern where mentee repeatedly fails to follow through, и manager responsibility to address directly, not avoid. Also: STAR-formula useful for документировать невыполнение как basis for harder conversation.
sections.when_to_apply: Для repeated pattern (2-3+ instances of non-follow-through), не one-off. Also adjust based on type of agreement: commitments related to core job vs aspirational growth.
sections.edge_cases: Не treat all agreements equally. Some agreements (deliverable on project) requires firm follow-through. Others (aspirational growth — `я хочу выступить на конференции`) more flexible — life happens. Не make mentee feel constantly evaluated.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q4]] SBI feedback; [[mentoring-interview#Q6]] resistance to feedback; [[mentoring-interview#Q16]] tracking progress.

options.label: B
options.text: Перестать ставить договорённости — раз не выполняются, бессмысленно.

sections.what_actually: Eliminating agreements removes structure for growth. Without commitments, mentorship becomes therapy session без actionable outcomes. Mentee's growth stalls, mentor's value diminishes.
sections.source_of_confusion: Manager frustration после repeated non-follow-through может lead to giving up. This is conflict avoidance dressed as `respecting autonomy`.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда successful mentorship would не require agreements. Реально every coaching framework (GROW, Co-Active, etc.) requires explicit agreements on next steps.
sections.how_it_should_be: Maintain agreement structure but adjust size, clarity, and follow-through process. Diagnose why agreements fail; address that. Don't eliminate accountability.

options.label: C
options.text: Жёстко наказать — снизить bonus или поставить unsatisfactory rating.

sections.what_actually: Punishment for failed mentorship commitments confuses two distinct things. Performance rating is about job performance (what's in role description); mentorship agreements often aspirational (growth beyond current role). Punishing for not completing aspirational growth = punishing for not exceeding expectations, which is unfair.
sections.source_of_confusion: Manager urges to enforce accountability lead to using formal tools (rating, bonus) where they don't apply.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда mentees would refuse aspirational commitments due to risk of punishment. Реально creates exactly that: people commit to less, growth stalls.
sections.how_it_should_be: Mentorship agreements separate from performance rating. Address through honest conversation, not formal punishment. Performance rating tied to role expectations, не growth aspirations.

options.label: D
options.text: Игнорировать — менти решит сам, когда готов выполнить.

sections.what_actually: Ignoring pattern of non-follow-through perpetuates pattern. Mentee learns that commitments are optional, mentor's expectations soft. Growth stalls; eventually manager либо frustrated либо team performance suffers.
sections.source_of_confusion: Conflict-averse managers prefer ignore. Also `respecting autonomy` rationalization.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда no follow-up after agreements would be effective. Реально accountability through gentle follow-up dramatically increases follow-through (Hawthorne effect plus social commitment).
sections.how_it_should_be: Gentle but consistent follow-up: `как идёт работа над X? Нужна help?`. This shows commitment matters without being punitive.

blocks.question_text: Вас попросили стать ментором для человека старше или опытнее вас (например, vice versa: вы tech lead, менти — senior с большим опытом в другой области). Как подойти?

options.label: A
options.text: Признать опыт явно, фокусироваться на том, что вы можете дать, больше вопросов чем советов, предложить взаимный обмен.

sections.explanation: Reverse mentorship (mentoring people с большим опытом или возрастом, чем у вас) — это специфический challenge, но reality в современных tech orgs, где fast technical change часто makes junior employees subject matter experts. Подход — четыре principles. Первый — explicit acknowledgement: открыто recognize their experience, не pretend to outrank them. `У вас 15 лет опыта в Java, я 5 — но specifically в этой компании и в этом modern stack я могу помочь с context`. Это disarms power dynamics confusion. Второй — focus on what you bring: новые технологии (modern frameworks, AI tooling), different perspective (cross-industry experience), structure (you may have processes they don't know), или просто context of this specific company/team. Не competition на overall expertise; complementary contribution. Третий — questions > advice ratio higher than usual. Опытный человек doesn't need you to tell answers; needs you to help them structure their own thinking. Active listening и probing questions provide value without claiming expertise you lack. Четвёртый — propose mutual exchange: explicit `я учу тебя X, ты учишь меня Y`. Это transforms hierarchical mentorship dynamic в peer learning relationship, что более comfortable для both и often more productive.
sections.example: Procter & Gamble (с 2014) launched formal reverse mentorship program: junior employees teach executives social media, AI, digital trends. BNY Mellon similar program. У Microsoft Сатья Наделла publically advocates `learn-it-all` instead of `know-it-all` culture, which welcomes reverse learning. Известный case: Jack Welch (GE CEO) had reverse mentor — younger employee teaching him internet basics в late 1990s.
sections.when_to_apply: При onboarding senior hires в new domain или company; при mentor-mentee age gap reversed (younger mentor, older mentee); при cross-functional mentorship где domains diverge (engineering mentor for designer, vice versa); при transformative tech changes where junior expertise leads.
sections.edge_cases: Не overclaim expertise you don't have. If menti asks deep question outside your knowledge, OK say `I don't know — let's figure out together`. Authenticity > performance. Also: watch for status anxiety, особенно от menti side — be explicit about value exchange to make it comfortable.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q1]] mentor vs coach; [[mentoring-interview#Q5]] coaching vs telling; [[mentoring-interview#Q23]] not imposing your style.

options.label: B
options.text: Притвориться более опытным — играть в `senior mentor` role.

sections.what_actually: Faking expertise очень quickly detected by experienced people. Они've seen real expertise и spot performance immediately. Result — instant loss of credibility и respect; relationship doesn't recover. Также: faking expertise leads вас give advice без real depth, which can mislead менти и cause real damage.
sections.source_of_confusion: Manager feels need to project authority and confidence. Also imposter syndrome in mentor может drive overcompensation.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда reverse mentorship programs would require fake hierarchy. Реально they explicitly work on authentic exchange.
sections.how_it_should_be: Authentic positioning: acknowledge their expertise, position yourself as bringing specific contribution, ask questions about their experience. Authenticity builds credibility; pretense destroys it.

options.label: C
options.text: Отказаться — `я не могу менторить человека опытнее себя`.

sections.what_actually: Refusing reverse mentorship misses opportunity for both sides. You miss exposure к senior perspective и chance to develop coaching skills with challenging context. Они miss specific contribution you can make. Also: organizational expectation often that managers mentor regardless of background.
sections.source_of_confusion: Self-doubt и cultural expectation that older = wiser create reluctance.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда new managers would never mentor anyone older. Реально это common reality в tech industry где team composition diverse в age и experience.
sections.how_it_should_be: Accept and adjust approach. Reverse mentorship is real and valuable. Adjust your contribution и framing.

options.label: D
options.text: Свести взаимодействие к minimum — `опытный сам разберётся`.

sections.what_actually: Disengaging from mentorship of senior person signals manager not interested or insufficient. Senior person interpretates as lack of care or competence. Also: their need для company-specific context, new tech, or external perspective remains unmet.
sections.source_of_confusion: Discomfort с senior people leads to passive avoidance.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда senior new hires would universally onboard successfully without manager involvement. Реально senior onboarding often requires more support than junior — different aspects, but real need.
sections.how_it_should_be: Active engagement with adjusted approach: more questions, more peer-style exchange, specific contribution focus. Lean in, не lean out.

blocks.question_text: Как избежать ловушки `делай как я` — навязывания собственного стиля менти?

options.label: A
options.text: Задавать вопросы вместо ответов, объяснять принципы вместо правил, принимать иначе обоснованные решения менти.

sections.explanation: `Делай как я` — это natural mentor tendency: you achieved something, you have clear way, you want others to follow same path. Но это ловушка по трём причинам. Первое — your approach is contextual: worked for your background, your team, your moment in time; не universally optimal. Второе — навязывание стиля убивает agency menti; they execute your approach без owning decision, что limits learning и creates dependency. Третье — diverse approaches often outperform homogeneous ones; team где everyone thinks like manager misses blind spots. Подход избежания этой ловушки — четыре practice. Первое — questions > answers ratio: вместо `вот так делай` — `как бы ты это решил?`, `какие тебе видны варианты?`, `что бы случилось, если бы X?`. Эти questions help menti articulate его reasoning, и в process они часто find better-for-them solution. Второе — explain principles, не rules: `почему важно testing` (catches regressions, documents intent, enables refactoring) vs `всегда пиши tests первым`. Principles transfer; rules don't. Третье — accept alternative decisions when they're well-reasoned. Если menti chose different solution than you'd choose, and arguments are valid — let them proceed. Только intervene если они making clearly bad call для wrong reasons. Четвёртое — encourage experiments and learning from mistakes. Mistakes within tolerable bounds — это growth fuel, не failure. Mentor's role — make safe environment for experimentation, не prevent all errors.
sections.example: Сократический метод (4th century BC) основан на вопросах, не лекциях. В современном tech: Pixar `braintrust` (Ed Catmull `Creativity Inc.`) — feedback through questions, не directives. У Toyota Production System `5 Whys` — diagnose through asking, не assertion. У Stripe engineering interviews focus on candidate's reasoning, не agreement с specific approach.
sections.when_to_apply: Для всех mentor-mentee interactions, особенно для technical decisions, design choices, и process work. Менее applicable для critical safety/security/compliance items where there are clear правильные answers.
sections.edge_cases: Не fall в opposite extreme — pure laissez-faire где никакого guidance. Some decisions clear (security, established team patterns); они need directive answer. Balance autonomy с appropriate guidance. Also: if menti consistently makes poor decisions, intervene with structure, не just keep asking questions.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q5]] coaching vs telling; [[mentoring-interview#Q1]] mentor not telling instructions; [[mentoring-interview#Q22]] questions over advice.

options.label: B
options.text: Подробно прописать checklist `как правильно работать` — менти следует ему step by step.

sections.what_actually: Detailed checklist для unique decisions kills judgment development. Менти учится мechanical следованию, не principled reasoning. Также: checklists work для repeated bounded tasks (pre-flight checklist в aviation), не для creative/judgment work (system design, mentorship).
sections.source_of_confusion: Atul Gawande `The Checklist Manifesto` popularized checklists, но specifically for bounded high-stakes routine tasks (surgery prep, aviation). Misapplied widely.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда creative knowledge work always proceduralized. Реально creative work resists procedure; great work emerges from judgment, не template-following.
sections.how_it_should_be: Use checklists для bounded routine tasks (deployment checklist, incident response checklist), но не для judgment-heavy work. Build menti's judgment through questions и principles.

options.label: C
options.text: Делать всё за менти — он быстрее научится наблюдая.

sections.what_actually: Doing for menti deprives them of practice opportunities. Watching is less effective learning than doing. Также: menti loses agency и motivation. Eventually they're either dependent or disengaged.
sections.source_of_confusion: Time pressure makes doing-it-yourself feel efficient. Also rescuing menti from struggle feels supportive.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда tutorial videos would teach как well as hands-on practice. Реально practice-based learning consistently outperforms observation-only.
sections.how_it_should_be: Pair programming where menti drives, you observe and ask questions. Or you do small part as example, then menti repeats. Always preserve menti's primary driver role.

options.label: D
options.text: Не вмешиваться вообще — пусть менти найдёт свой путь.

sections.what_actually: Complete non-intervention abandons mentorship responsibility. Menti может get lost in dead-ends, repeat preventable mistakes, или make decisions с serious negative consequences. Также menti expects guidance from mentor; absence reads as disengagement.
sections.source_of_confusion: Reaction to `do as I do` problem может swing too far other way.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда mentorship would be just casual conversation без structure. Реально mentorship involves active guidance, just не imposed style.
sections.how_it_should_be: Active guidance through questions и principles, не imposition of style. Mentor stays involved and present; just changes mode from directive to inquiring.

blocks.question_text: Как оценить эффективность вашего менторства?

options.label: A
options.text: Скорость роста менти, самостоятельные решения, фидбэк менти другим, NPS-like вопросы, качественные признаки (proactive 1:1 requests, decisions referencing your conversations).

sections.explanation: Mentorship effectiveness тяжело measure quantitatively, но possible через combination metrics. Первое — growth velocity relative to expected track: менти progresses через levels faster или at expected pace? Promo timelines, scope expansion, new capabilities acquired — все evidence. Второе — autonomous decision quality: менти makes more independent decisions over time, и quality of those decisions improves? Reduced dependency на mentor for routine choices = good progress. Третье — menti's mentorship of others: if your menti starts mentoring junior engineers и giving good feedback (`мне нравится твой code review style — у тебя есть структура`), это suggests он absorbed valuable practices. Skill transfer — sign of deep learning. Четвёртое — direct NPS-like assessment: ask menti `насколько полезны наши 1:1?` и `что бы изменил?`. Не one-time; quarterly или semi-annual. Open feedback. Пятое — qualitative signs: menti proactively requests meetings, shares thinking ahead of time (`hey, перед нашим 1:1 think about X`), references mentor conversations в decisions (`когда мы говорили о Y, я подумал`). Эти behavioural signs показывают mentorship integrated в menti's growth, не just calendar appointments. Шестое — for long-term: alumni feedback. Когда menti уходит из company, what do they tell others о mentorship experience? Long after relationship ended, do они reach out, recommend you, или mention as influential? Это ultimate measure of mentorship impact.
sections.example: Many tech executives publicly credit specific mentors years after relationship ended (Sundar Pichai mentioning Eric Schmidt, Sheryl Sandberg mentioning Larry Summers). У Bridgewater Ray Dalio implemented `dot collector` system that includes specific feedback on people's decisions и mentorship quality. У Camille Fournier `The Manager's Path` chapter on `the great manager` describes both quantitative и qualitative signs.
sections.when_to_apply: Quarterly self-assessment as mentor; annual review of menti relationships; before major decisions affecting menti (promo committee, role assignment); when mentorship not seeming to land и diagnosis needed.
sections.edge_cases: Не over-measure. Mentorship is partly relational; чрезмерное measurement makes both sides feel they're being evaluated, что reduces authenticity. Use these as periodic check-ins, не constant evaluation. Также: short-term metrics (3 months) less reliable than long-term (1 year+); pattern emerges over time.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q10]] performance review; [[mentoring-interview#Q16]] tracking progress; [[mentoring-interview#Q25]] mentorship failures.

options.label: B
options.text: Количество проведённых 1:1 — это objective metric.

sections.what_actually: 1:1 count is activity metric, не outcome metric. You can have 100 meaningless 1:1s или 10 transformative ones; counts don't differentiate. Также: focus on quantity perversely incentivizes shallow but frequent interactions.
sections.source_of_confusion: Easy to measure (calendar count). Manager metrics dashboards often include 1:1 frequency.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда managers с highest 1:1 frequency would have best mentorship outcomes. Реально quality > quantity by large margin.
sections.how_it_should_be: 1:1 frequency useful as baseline (`are 1:1 happening at all?`), но real measure is outcomes: growth, decisions, behaviour change.

options.label: C
options.text: Спросить менти, доволен ли он — субъективная оценка достаточна.

sections.what_actually: Satisfaction survey only captures one dimension и subject to bias. Menti может be satisfied with comfortable mentorship that's not pushing growth, or dissatisfied with effective mentorship that's appropriately challenging. Single-dimension measure inadequate.
sections.source_of_confusion: NPS measurement popular in product context, и naively applied to mentorship.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда happy menti = effective mentorship. Реально they often correlate but не always; sometimes hard mentor relationships produce best growth.
sections.how_it_should_be: Satisfaction is one signal among several. Combine with growth metrics, decision quality, skill transfer signs.

options.label: D
options.text: Эффективность менторства невозможно оценить — это soft skill.

sections.what_actually: Mentorship effectiveness measurable, just не through simple quantitative metrics alone. Combination of qualitative и behavioural signs, плюс growth outcomes, дают reliable assessment. Saying `can't measure` abdicates accountability for improvement.
sections.source_of_confusion: Tendency to dismiss soft skills as immeasurable, opposite to obsession with metricizing everything.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда mentor effectiveness couldn't improve through feedback. Реально mentor skills improve dramatically with conscious practice и feedback, suggesting measurable underlying dimensions.
sections.how_it_should_be: Multi-dimensional assessment: growth, autonomy, skill transfer, satisfaction, qualitative behavioural signs. Use for personal improvement and accountability.

blocks.question_text: Расскажите case, когда ваше менторство не дало результата. Что вы узнали?

options.label: A
options.text: Honest STAR-story с реальным failure и конкретным learning о валидации интересов менти, calibration целей, или ограничениях менторства.

sections.explanation: Эта question — это behavioural interview classic, testing self-awareness, growth mindset, и реалистичное понимание mentorship. Хороший ответ имеет STAR structure с real failure и concrete learning. Пример: `Я ментрил инженера год с целью senior. Я давал stretch projects, проводил еженедельные 1:1, помогал с visibility. Через 12 месяцев он сказал, что хочет staying на текущем уровне как deep specialist, не идти broader. Action assessment: я никогда явно не asked если он wants this path — я предположил по signals и invest accordingly. Result: год effort на goal которая не его. Learning: первая question в any mentorship — "чего ты сам хочешь?", не "куда тебя надо вырастить". С тех пор начинаю каждые new mentorship pair с explicit career direction conversation`. Принципы хорошего failure-story. Первое — real failure: не fake humility (`мой failure был, что я слишком много помогал`). Реальный mistake с реальными consequences. Второе — system thinking: failure framed as flawed approach, не personality flaw of menti. (`Я предположил вместо asked`, не `он был неправильным candidate`). Третье — concrete learning: specific behaviour change в future. Не abstract (`я научился listen better`); concrete (`я начинаю каждое mentorship с explicit career direction question`). Четвёртое — application demonstrated: что вы делали differently после learning? Showing learning integrated в practice, не just acknowledged. Common failure modes mentorship, which good answers explore: assumed direction без validation, mismatch in pace expectations, не recognized burnout vs lack of motivation, kept pushing когда menti не engaged, didn't recognize sponsorship vs mentorship gap, treated menti as version of yourself.
sections.example: У Camille Fournier `The Manager's Path` openly discusses mentorship failures. Lara Hogan `Resilient Management` similarly. Best engineering leaders publicly share failures (e.g., Charity Majors блог posts о management mistakes). Interview answers с this depth differentiate strong leadership candidates from those who give superficial responses.
sections.when_to_apply: Для behavioural interviews при roles с people responsibility. Также useful self-reflection exercise: что был your biggest mentorship failure, и что you learned. Don't wait для interview to think about this.
sections.edge_cases: Не share story that's actually positive в disguise (`my failure was caring too much` — fake humility). Также: не throw menti under bus (`he was just lazy`). Take responsibility for mentor's role в outcome.
sections.related: [[mentoring-interview#Q12]] no growth ambition; [[mentoring-interview#Q14]] plateau stuck; [[mentoring-interview#Q24]] mentorship effectiveness.

options.label: B
options.text: Сказать `у меня не было неудач в менторстве` — это показывает уверенность.

sections.what_actually: Claiming no mentorship failures destroys interview credibility instantly. Every experienced mentor has failures — anyone claiming otherwise either inexperienced или lacks self-awareness. Interviewer вiews this as red flag in both directions.
sections.source_of_confusion: Misguided belief that admitting weakness hurts interview. Реально admitting concrete failures with learning shows maturity и growth mindset.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда experienced mentors universally claim perfect record. Реально best leaders publicly share failures (Bridgewater Ray Dalio's `principles` is largely about learning from mistakes).
sections.how_it_should_be: Share real failure с lesson. Vulnerability + learning >>> performed perfection.

options.label: C
options.text: Свалить всё на менти: `он не хотел учиться`.

sections.what_actually: Blaming menti shows lack of ownership и self-awareness. Mentor responsible for engagement, adjusting approach, recognizing fit issues. Blaming читается как `I'd repeat same mistakes` because no learning identified в self.
sections.source_of_confusion: Defensive reaction protect ego. Also reflects shifted-responsibility thinking common в weak leadership.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда blaming employees was effective management practice. Реально это recognized antipattern in leadership literature.
sections.how_it_should_be: Own mentor's role в outcome. Even if menti contributed to failure, focus what you could've done differently.

options.label: D
options.text: Рассказать generic story without specifics — `один менти как-то не вырос`.

sections.what_actually: Generic story without specifics suggests либо no real reflection happened, либо unwillingness to share details. Interviewer reads as either lack of self-awareness или evasion. Specific examples с numbers, timelines, и concrete actions — это hallmarks of genuine learning.
sections.source_of_confusion: Privacy concerns ('не хочу talking specific о former menti'). Reasonable but can be addressed through anonymization without losing detail.
sections.if_it_were_true: Тогда vague behavioural answers passed interviews regularly. Реально they consistently raise red flags для experienced interviewers.
sections.how_it_should_be: Specific story с anonymized details: timeline, situation, your action, outcome, learning. Privacy maintained, specificity preserved.
